output.text: The science fair filled the gymnasium with tables of volcanoes, circuit boards, and plant experiments, and the judges moved slowly from booth to booth. Assume that Uma is the team captain. Everyone gathered near the entrance early that morning, checking their poster boards and rehearsing their explanations one more time before the doors opened to visitors. Milo arrived before Mina. The organizers had set up a registration table where each student wrote their project title on a name tag, and the line moved quickly since only a handful of students had shown up so far. Mina arrived before Gia. Gia is younger than Uma by almost a full year, though the two of them worked on a shared display about renewable energy sources for part of the semester. Wren brought the first-aid kit. Uma stands slightly taller than Milo, which made it easier for her to hang the banner above their group table without needing a stool. Milo arrived before Gia. Mina ranked higher than Wren in last years regional competition, a fact that came up while they were comparing notes on judging criteria near the snack table. Throughout the afternoon, the five friends helped each other adjust their displays, offering suggestions about lighting and labeling. By the time the judges announced the winners, everyone had grown a little hoarse from explaining their projects again and again, but the sense of accomplishment in the room was easy to see on every face as families began packing up their tables for the evening.
